Issued at 308 PM EST Sun Nov 8 2026

Pattern Synopsis/Forecast: Wavy...Pacific-dominant pattern continues 
across North America...with a short wave train extending from New 
England out into the Pacific basin south of the Aleutian Islands. 
One "car" in this train is crossing northern Ontario and the upper 
Great Lakes today...with strong height falls also progressing across 
the Pacific Northwest/British Columbia/Alberta.  Next round of low 
level cold air advection also spreading across the upper Lakes 
today...in the wake of a cold/occluded front attached to 999mb 
surface low over far northern Ontario.    

Short wave energy slips across the Great Lakes today with low 
amplitude short wave ridging for Monday.  Remnants of short wave 
energy moving through western Canada this morning forecast to cross 
Michigan Tuesday...associated weak surface reflection passes north 
of Lake Superior but another cold front moves through Michigan 
probably early in the day.  Large scale pattern still trending 
toward a more amplified +PNA/+EPO starting Wednesday as effects from 
a strengthening trough over the eastern Pacific ripple downstream. 
Will be watching a couple pieces of energy upstream...one over 
central Canada and a second digging into the Midwest.  Both waves 
will help dig out a long wave trough across eastern North America 
for midweek: the latter feature is forecast to spin up a cyclone 
over the Midwest Wednesday.  Some better consensus on this system 
tracking from the mid Mississippi Valley to somewhere along/north of 
the Ohio River by Thursday morning...then possibly transitioning to 
secondary east coast cyclogenesis.  Resultant broad upper cyclone 
may keep the Great Lakes in its (cold) grip into next weekend.    

Primary Forecast Concerns:  

Lake effect showers tonight/breezy: Synoptic moisture and decreasing 
stability over Lake Superior generating showers spreading into 
eastern Upper this afternoon.  Also expect to increasing shower 
coverage over northern portions of Lake Michigan/Lake Huron as 
increased low level moisture in the form of an southeastward 
advancing Sc deck arrives.  Shower probabilities will be more 
limited south of M-72/west of US-131 with a shallower CBL expected 
(lacking a longer effective fetch). Inversion highs should drop as 
tonight wears on with increasing downward forcing...so would expect 
shower coverage to decrease as well though will be a little slower 
than guidance would suggest given typical "lake convective inertia 
issues" for lack of a better scientific term.  Gusty winds 
eventually coming from the northwest are expected into this 
evening...gusts 20 to 30mph with gusts 30 to 40mph around Whitefish 
Bay and along the US-23 corridor north of Thunder Bay off Lake 
Huron.  Winds are expected to diminish overnight as surface ridge 
axis slide into Michigan and gradient relaxes. 

Impacts of a system passing south of Michigan Wednesday and 
beyond...turning colder along with precipitation chances (synoptic 
Wednesday/lake effect Thursday-Friday):  Short wave trough will be 
over the upper Midwest Wednesday...spinning up a surface cyclone in 
response near the Iowa/Missouri border tracking east/southeast along 
the Ohio River by Thursday morning.  Some synoptic precipitation 
along deformation zone of this system possible across Lower Michigan 
Wednesday...but coldest air of the fall season so far arrives 
Thursday (especially given how downright balmy it has been since the 
start of October).  850mb temperatures may drop to or below -8C... 
providing a good lake convective set up.  At this point boundary 
layer flow looks to be a bit east of north...so precipitation 
chances will be more likely closer to the shorelines.  850mb 
temperatures that cold would certainly suggest some snow 
probabilities even close to the lakes; snow probabilities are pretty 
small for right now but suspect they will improve as the week 
progresses.
